caption: Figure 1. Login screen providing university email and password fields, account creation and password recovery.
Figure 2. Login validation identifies missing email and password fields.
Figure 3. Password recovery form requests a reset link by university email. Completion of a new-password flow requires access to the recipient mailbox and is not captured.
Figure 4. Account creation form collects the student's full name, university email and a password meeting the stated minimum requirements.
Figure 5. Registration validation identifies a missing full name and email and a password that does not meet the minimum rules.
Figure 6. Successful registration opens Skill Passport onboarding, beginning with identity, major, study year and an optional headline.
Figure 7. Skill Passport onboarding allows students to select skills, proficiency levels and interests.
Figure 8. Final Skill Passport onboarding step provides weekly availability, preferred days and three profile visibility choices.
Figure 9. Passport visibility choices are Everyone at Takatuf, Teams you apply to and Only you, with an explanation of each option.
Figure 10. Opportunity discovery home has search and category filters; no opportunities were available after onboarding.
Figure 11. Afnan's saved Skill Passport displays identity, advanced Kotlin, six hours of weekly availability and public visibility.
Figure 12. Passport visibility can be changed after onboarding using the three-option editor.
Figure 13. The owner-facing Passport shows the saved Teams you apply to visibility setting. Access enforcement for another account remains to be demonstrated.
Figure 14. Experience editing supports a role or project, organization, period and optional description.
Figure 15. Posting offers project recruitment, event-linked teammate requests, and competition or hackathon sharing.
Figure 16. Project recruitment form includes outcome, reusable role templates and team size.
Figure 17. Publishing an empty project highlights required name, outcome and recruitment roles.
Figure 18. Selecting Mobile developer adds a reusable role template with suggested skills and one vacancy.
Figure 19. Role customization supports a title, skill tags and open places.
Figure 20. Project recruitment displays current team size, two open places, weekly commitment and duration choices.
Figure 21. Successfully published project details show the customized two vacancies, outcome and commitment. The owner receives Review applicants.
Figure 22. Owner applicant review initially shows no applicants, with All and Shortlisted tabs.
Figure 23. The listing owner can edit or close recruitment using the details menu.
Figure 24. Owner editing loads the existing project name, outcome and customized role.
Figure 25. Discovery lists the published demonstration project, requested role, weekly commitment and the Yours label.
Figure 26. Event sharing supports Competition and Hackathon types, organizer, official source and dates.
Figure 27. Empty event submission highlights the required name, organizer, official link and dates.
Figure 28. Event creation includes team-size rules, eligibility, attendance format, location and descriptive details.
